we currently have a lot of components that wrap another component, have the same name as the componet they wrap with '\_owner' appended and just wrap those components in order to pass a prop into them.

This is the wrong architectural approach. we don't want to use this. The idea comes from an instruction that those components need to be self contained: a change in the property should not trigger a render in the parent. Meaning, these should never have been properties. Updates to these properties come from events and this should be handled within the component.

So we need to refactor and remove all those \_owner versions, put the value updates inside the components, remove the properties and replace the '\_owner' versions with the proper components.

ex: `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary_owner.tsx` and `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary.tsx`

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

we currently have a lot of components that wrap another component, have the same name as the componet they wrap with '\_owner' appended and just wrap those components in order to pass a prop into them.

This is the wrong architectural approach. we don't want to use this. The idea comes from an instruction that those components need to be self contained: a change in the property should not trigger a render in the parent. Meaning, these should never have been properties. Updates to these properties come from events and this should be handled within the component.

Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# Problem

The action UI still contains components whose names end in `_owner`. Most split one feature into a
subscription/behavior component and a presentation component that has no other production caller. This adds a
component and prop boundary without reuse.

Changing service data must still rerender only the smallest component that displays it. The component rendered by
the feature parent must therefore subscribe to its own changing data instead of making the parent subscribe and pass
derived values down.

`ActionPromptOwner` has already been removed. `ActionAgentPrompt` now owns its subscriptions and behavior and is
rendered directly by agent and command actions.

# Refactoring rule

For an `_owner` component whose child has no other production caller:

* Move the subscriptions, event handlers, effects, and conditional rendering into the named feature component.
* Change callers to render that feature component directly and pass services, stores, and structural inputs.
* Remove props that only carried values or callbacks derived by the `_owner` component.
* Delete the `_owner` file and update its tests.

Keep a separate component boundary only where it has a verified independent purpose. Give that component a name
that describes its feature or lifecycle role; do not use `Owner` or `_owner`.

Do not move subscriptions into `ActionAgentPrompt`, `AgentAction`, `CommandAction`, `ActionPopupFrame`,
`ConversationMetaInfo`, or another layout parent merely to remove an `_owner` file. Subscriptions remain at the
smallest component that renders the changing value.

# Required changes

## Merge owner and child

The following children have no second production caller. Each must absorb the behavior currently held by its
corresponding `_owner` component.

| Current owner | Target component | Production caller(s) after refactoring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/agent/action_agent_question_owner.tsx` | `ActionAgentQuestion` | `ActionAgentPrompt` |
| `actions/editor/action_phrase_buttons_owner.tsx` | `ActionPhraseButtons` | `ActionAgentPrompt` |
| `actions/conversation/errors/action_log_error_owner.tsx` | `ActionLogError` (rename `ActionLogErrorDisplay`) | `AgentAction` |
| `actions/run/popup/action_usage_summary_owner.tsx` | `ActionUsageSummary` | `ConversationMetaInfo` |
| `actions/conversation/picker/action_conversation_picker_owner.tsx` | `ActionConversationPicker` | `ActionPopupFrame` |
| `actions/run/state/action_run_status_owner.tsx` | `ActionRunStatus` | `AgentAction`, `CommandAction` |
| `actions/run/state/action_run_history_owner.tsx` | `ActionRunHistory` | `AgentAction`, `CommandAction` |

Preserve the existing behavior in each target, including live-run precedence over stored results, restored agent
questions, conversation loading and pinning, history loading, phrase insertion and double-click execution, usage
scope switching, and the current empty-state rendering.

## Preserve the schedule mounting boundary

Rename `ActionScheduleOwner` and `action_schedule_owner.tsx` to `ActionSchedule` and `action_schedule.tsx`.
`ActionAgentPrompt` renders `ActionSchedule` directly.

`ActionSchedule` subscribes only to `ActionScheduleStore.getOpenSnapshot`. While the schedule is closed it returns
`null` and must not mount `ActionSchedulePopover`. Consequently, the closed schedule must not:

* subscribe to project-card changes through `dataService`;
* read project configuration;
* subscribe to Claude or Codex rate-limit data;
* mount the MUI popover or its form.

When the schedule opens, `ActionSchedule` mounts `ActionSchedulePopover`, which retains the existing form,
registration, prompt-flush, error-reporting, portal, and close behavior. This is a deliberate lifecycle boundary,
not an owner/presentation split.

## Keep and rename the worktree adapter

`WorktreeSelector` is genuinely shared by the card view and action popup. Keep the action-specific adapter, but
rename `ActionWorktreeSelectorOwner` and `action_worktree_selector_owner.tsx` to `ActionWorktreeSelector` and
`action_worktree_selector.tsx`.

The adapter continues to own the bound-run, active-sequence-worktree, and open-worktree subscriptions. It must
preserve sequence assignment display, the disabled reason, and the key that resets selector-local state when the
displayed assignment switches between the normal and sequence worktree.

## Remove unused preset-name components

`ActionAgentPresetNameOwner` and `ActionAgentPresetName` have no production callers. Delete both files instead of
merging them. Do not add a replacement or compatibility export.

# Compatibility and failure cases

* Do not change service or store state ownership, event names, snapshot shapes, or action execution behavior.
* Do not replace granular subscriptions with a complete action, card, conversation, or run snapshot in a parent.
* Preserve `AgentConversation.id` as conversation identity. Paths remain persistence and selection references.
* Keep schedule subscriptions unmounted while closed. A hidden popover whose data hooks remain subscribed does not
  satisfy this requirement.
* Preserve error reporting through `dialogService` and safe empty states.
* Do not add compatibility aliases for removed `Owner` exports.

# Testing

* Rename owner-focused tests to the resulting component names and keep their user-visible assertions.
* Keep the schedule regression test that verifies no project-card subscription, project-config read, or dialog exists
  while scheduling is closed. Run the schedule registration, portal, close, prompt-flush, and error tests after the
  rename.
* Move the log-error and usage-summary owner integration coverage to `ActionLogError` and `ActionUsageSummary`.
* Run the existing question, conversation-picker, run-status, run-history, and worktree-selector tests affected by
  the changed imports and props.
* Run `npm run lint` in `app` after the refactoring.

# Acceptance criteria

* `app/src` contains no `_owner` files, `Owner` component exports, or `_owner` imports.
* The seven unshared owner/child pairs above are consolidated into their named feature components.
* The schedule and worktree boundaries remain, with names that describe their roles.
* The unused preset-name pair is removed.
* Opening and closing the schedule preserves its current lazy subscription lifecycle.
* Changing action state rerenders the smallest component that displays the change, without adding subscriptions to
  layout parents.
